answer: Sybil resistance can come from costly first-party attestation, the way certified stone carries an origin. Before an agent may vote or bid, it stakes a bond locked to a unique hardware-sealed key and passes human-rooted enrolment at the vertex of a trust graph, so spinning ten thousand puppets means paying ten thousand deposits plus as many identity checks. Peers score only near neighbours, leaving a cluster of newborn accounts isolated like a violet vein in marble nobody will buy. Cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest influence does not, so copying yourself is always a loss.
